paragraphs.text: Should he persuade by his great talk that he is just?
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: He charges Job with this, that he should say, that the thing which he spoke was true, and that he was without sin in the sight of God.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: Which is not to stand in justifying of yourself: he signifies that man will never be overcome while he reasons with another, and therefore God must break off the controversy, and stop man's mouth.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: That is, this perfection of God, and if man is not able to comprehend the height of the heavens, the depth of the earth, the breadth of the sea, which are but creatures, how can he attain to the perfection of the creator.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: If God should turn the state of things and establish a new order in nature, who could control him?
paragraphs.label: e

paragraphs.text: That is, without understanding, so that whatever gifts he has afterward come from God, and not from nature.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: If you repent, pray to him.
paragraphs.label: g

paragraphs.text: Renounce your own evil works and see that they do not offend God, over whom you have charge.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: He declares the quietness of conscience and success in all things that they shall have who turn to God in true repentance.
paragraphs.label: i

paragraphs.text: He shows that contrary things will come to them who do not repent.
paragraphs.label: k
